title: Build your path into tech
instruction: Talk about what you’re learning, explain a small project and ask for useful help

vocabulary.example: I use a tutorial to learn one new feature.
vocabulary.exampleTranslation: Eu uso um tutorial para aprender uma funcionalidade nova.
vocabulary.classAudioText: a tutorial. I use a tutorial to learn one new feature.

vocabulary.example: I check the documentation when I need an explanation.
vocabulary.exampleTranslation: Eu consulto a documentação quando preciso de uma explicação.
vocabulary.classAudioText: documentation. I check the documentation when I need an explanation.

vocabulary.example: The error message tells me what went wrong.
vocabulary.exampleTranslation: A mensagem de erro me diz o que deu errado.
vocabulary.classAudioText: an error message. The error message tells me what went wrong.

vocabulary.example: My practice project is a task-list app.
vocabulary.exampleTranslation: Meu projeto de prática é um aplicativo de lista de tarefas.
vocabulary.classAudioText: a practice project. My practice project is a task-list app.

vocabulary.example: My study plan has three short sessions this week.
vocabulary.exampleTranslation: Meu plano de estudos tem três sessões curtas nesta semana.
vocabulary.classAudioText: a study plan. My study plan has three short sessions this week.

vocabulary.example: My portfolio shows projects I can explain.
vocabulary.exampleTranslation: Meu portfólio mostra projetos que eu consigo explicar.
vocabulary.classAudioText: a portfolio. My portfolio shows projects I can explain.

dialogue.speaker: Kim
dialogue.text: What are you learning at the moment?
dialogue.translation: O que você está aprendendo no momento?
dialogue.displayText: What are you learning at the moment?

dialogue.speaker: Ana
dialogue.text: I’m learning to build small web applications. I’m working on a task-list app.
dialogue.translation: Estou aprendendo a desenvolver pequenos aplicativos web. Estou trabalhando em um aplicativo de lista de tarefas
dialogue.displayText: I’m learning to build small web applications. I’m working on a task-list app

dialogue.speaker: Kim
dialogue.text: What can someone do with your app?
dialogue.translation: O que uma pessoa consegue fazer com o seu aplicativo?
dialogue.displayText: What can someone do with your app?

dialogue.speaker: Ana
dialogue.text: They can add tasks and mark them as complete. I want the tasks to stay there after a refresh.
dialogue.translation: As pessoas podem adicionar tarefas e marcá-las como concluídas. Eu quero que as tarefas continuem lá depois de atualizar a página
dialogue.displayText: They can add tasks and mark them as complete. I want the tasks to stay there after a refresh

dialogue.speaker: Kim
dialogue.text: How will you practice this week?
dialogue.translation: Como você vai praticar nesta semana?
dialogue.displayText: How will you practice this week?

dialogue.speaker: Ana
dialogue.text: I’ll build one small feature, test it and write down anything I don’t understand.
dialogue.translation: Vou desenvolver uma pequena funcionalidade, testá-la e anotar tudo o que eu não entender
dialogue.displayText: I’ll build one small feature, test it and write down anything I don’t understand

dialogueQuestions.hint: Think about the purpose of her practice project
dialogueQuestions.answer: She is building a task-list app

dialogueQuestions.prompt: What should happen after a page refresh?
dialogueQuestions.answer: The tasks should still be there after a refresh

dialogueQuestions.prompt: What three actions does Ana plan for this week?
dialogueQuestions.answer: She plans to build one feature, test it and write down what she does not understand

listening.title: Listen and answer
listening.instruction: A change to your study session. Listen to both notes. Questions 1–3 refer to the first note; questions 4–6 refer to the second
listening.greeting: A quick change for our next study session

notes.text: A quick update about our next study session. We’ll use audio only, so we won’t share screens or code. Choose one feature from your practice project. Explain what it does and who would use it.
notes.speaker: Owen

notes.text: One more thing: tell me what you tested and what you still want to improve. Send me a short voice note before we meet. If you’re stuck, include the error message and one thing you’ve already tried.
notes.speaker: Owen

questions.prompt: How will the next session work?
questions.hint: Listen for what people can hear and see
questions.answer: It will be audio only, without screen sharing or code

questions.prompt: What should you choose from your practice project?
questions.hint: Choose something small enough to explain

questions.prompt: Which two things about the feature should you explain?
questions.hint: Think about its purpose and its users
questions.answer: You should explain what it does and who would use it

questions.prompt: What should you say about your progress?
questions.hint: Think about testing and the next improvement
questions.answer: You should say what you tested and what you still want to improve

questions.prompt: What does Owen ask you to send before the session?
questions.answer: He asks for a short voice note

questions.prompt: If you are stuck, which two details should you include?
questions.hint: Explain the problem and an action you have already taken
questions.answer: You should include the error message and one thing you have already tried

freeConversationInstruction: Talk about learning something new, projects you enjoy and asking for help. Follow each other’s ideas

oralPages.title: Make time to build something
oralPages.instruction: Use the example week to plan one realistic study session with your teacher

turns.question: When could you fit a short study session into your week?
turns.cue: Choose a realistic time in your own routine
turns.hint: I could study… / I have time…
turns.model: I could study for thirty minutes after work on Wednesday

turns.question: What would you work on during that session?
turns.cue: Choose one small task
turns.model: I’d work on keeping the tasks after a refresh

turns.question: How would you know you had made progress?
turns.cue: Name a result you could show
turns.model: I’d be able to refresh the page and still see the tasks

oralPages.title: Tell me what you’re working on
oralPages.instruction: Explain your own learning goal, project and next step. Use the task-list example if you prefer

turns.question: What are you learning at the moment?
turns.cue: Explain your current focus
turns.model: I’m learning how to build and test small web applications

turns.question: What are you building to practice it?
turns.cue: Name a project and explain its purpose
turns.model: I’m building a task-list app to help people organise their day

turns.question: What is one small goal for your next study session?
turns.cue: Choose a realistic next step
turns.model: Next time, I’ll save the task list and test it after a refresh

oralPages.title: Turn a tutorial into a small project
oralPages.instruction: Use the task-list example. Choose one feature to build, explain how someone uses it and suggest a test

turns.question: What is one useful feature you could build first?
turns.cue: Choose one small feature
turns.model: I’d start with adding a task

turns.question: How would someone use that feature?
turns.cue: Explain an action and its result
turns.model: They would enter a title and select Add task. The new task would appear in the list

turns.question: How could you check that it works?
turns.cue: Describe one simple test
turns.model: I’d add a new task and check that it appears only once

oralPages.title: Describe the problem before asking for help
oralPages.instruction: Compare the task list before and after refresh. Explain the expected result, the problem and a useful next step

turns.question: What did you expect to happen after refreshing the page?
turns.cue: Describe the expected result
turns.model: I expected the tasks to stay in the list

turns.question: What actually happened?
turns.cue: Describe the result you can see
turns.model: After I refreshed the page, the list was empty

turns.question: What could you try before asking for help?
turns.cue: Suggest one check, then ask a specific question
turns.hint: I could check… / Could you help me…?
turns.model: I could check how the app saves tasks. Could you help me understand why they disappear?

oralPages.title: Check in with your mentor
oralPages.instruction: Look at another small practice project: a Login screen. Ask your teacher to check what should happen and how to test it

turns.question: What should this form do when the details are correct?
turns.cue: Explain the purpose of the form and its button
turns.model: The user enters an email address and a password. The button should sign them in

turns.question: How could you check the error message safely?
turns.cue: Use a test account rather than real personal details
turns.model: I’d use a test account and try an incorrect password

turns.question: What feedback would help you improve this project?
turns.cue: Ask one clear question about the layout or message
turns.model: Could you check the layout? Is the error message clear enough to explain what went wrong?

oralPages.title: Choose something you can explain
oralPages.instruction: Use the portfolio draft or your own project. Explain what works, what you built and one improvement

turns.question: Which project would you choose to show someone?
turns.cue: Choose one project and give a reason
turns.model: I’d choose the task-list app because I can explain how someone uses it

turns.question: What could you show them in your repository or demo?
turns.cue: Point to something you can demonstrate
turns.model: I can show the frontend adding a task and the files in my repository

turns.question: What would you improve before sharing it?
turns.cue: Name one useful next step
turns.model: Before I share it, I’ll test what happens after a refresh and add a short explanation

oralPages.title: Reply without showing your screen
oralPages.instruction: Answer your teacher aloud as if the next study session had started. Explain one feature and ask for useful help

turns.question: Which feature did you choose, and who is it for?
turns.cue: Explain a feature and its users
turns.model: My feature saves tasks. It helps people organise their day

turns.question: What have you tested, and what do you still want to improve?
turns.cue: Describe a result and one next step
turns.hint: I tested… / I still want to…
turns.model: I tested adding a task. I still want to keep the tasks after a refresh

turns.question: What help do you need from me?
turns.cue: Give useful context and ask a question
turns.hint: I tried… / Could you help me…?
turns.model: I checked the error message. Could you help me understand why the list is not saved?
